name: Meet for Slack
description: A Slack app: type `/meet` in any channel or DM to generate a Google Meet link. It opens with the right Google account and sets everyone's Slack status to "On a call" (company-stated). It says it's approved by Google and Slack and trusted by thousands of teams. 60-day free trial, free for up to 3 people, then $50 / $150 / $500 per year by workspace size (company-stated, yearly pricing). Founded Jun 2023, US.

mentions.evidence: ~$4,173 MRR (−6.0% L30), 387 active subscriptions (~$11/mo average, my calculation), ~$6,426 L30 (+135.2%), ~$46,394 last 12 months, ~$148,161 all-time, ~95% L30 profit margin. Revenue synced Oct 8, 2026 ~07:12 Warsaw (05:12 UTC).
mentions.indieAngle: Find two tools that are always used together but don't talk, and charge $50–$150 a year per workspace. For PL teams that could be Slack/Teams ↔ Fakturownia/inFakt (an invoice-paid ping in the channel), or Teams ↔ Google Meet. Each one is a small app, listed in a marketplace, that never needs marketing beyond the directory.

whyItPrints: It's glue between two tools every startup already pays for, and it fixes the annoying wrong-account problem. A tiny price nobody questions, 95% margin, and distribution through the Slack App Directory. L30 runs above MRR because annual renewals land in lumps (my inference).
